findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a worker commits a template change, runs forge sync, and leaves the generated copies uncommitted. The check compares the working-tree files through sync.differing, while close reviews and pushes HEAD; with an unchanged Forge pin, close.py:826 skips the existing committed-output check. Review and CI can therefore receive the stale copies. The tracked-file filter also omits newly generated guide files and committed deletions; for example, plain_english.py:16-20 generates copies for new security-audit template files. The full unmet item is: Before a fix or task round is handed back as done, Forge regenerates the synced guide copies when the template changed in the branch, or close stops locally with forge sync as the next step before any review or CI wait.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an active branch is closed after the default branch upgrades Forge. close.py:201 merges the upgrade, but the new call parses forge.toml and renders guides with the old running release before close.py:247 hands off to the new pin. A new setting can be rejected as unknown, and updated guides can be compared against the old release's templates. The existing mid-run pin test at tests/test_running_commands_follow_changed_forge_pin.py:151-170 exercises the former case and now encounters this check before the handoff.
findings.title: Functional: Hand off to the new pin before rendering guides

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - the coordinator runs forge close from the main checkout while the fix or task lives in its own worktree. close.py:85-87 resolves that worktree, but this refusal tells the caller only to run forge sync. In the main checkout that command either has nothing to update or refuses to write on the default branch, leaving the item's guides stale and close blocked. This earlier refusal also changes the output expected by the existing upgrade regression at tests/test_upgrade_synced.py:35-41.
findings.title: Functional: Name the worktree in the sync next step

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a new or previously adopted client repo uses close after upgrading Forge. Both parameters force the fixture to repo = "forge-source"; the previous case copies only two old guide files and syncs them before close. Neither exercises the installed client-package path at sync.py:603, so disabling the check for every client would still pass the named proof. The required new-client and earlier-adopted-client behavior needs command-level coverage.
